questions.explain: The ortho methyl group twists –COOH out of the ring plane, cutting off the resonance that weakens benzoic acid, so o-toluic acid (pKa 3.9) is stronger than benzoic acid (4.2) despite the +I methyl group.

questions.q: The correct order of basicity is
questions.explain: An ortho group crowds the bulkier –NH₃⁺ formed on protonation (steric inhibition of protonation), so o-toluidine is the weakest base; the para methyl only releases electrons.

questions.q: Which ortho-substituted benzoic acid is a WEAKER acid than benzoic acid?
questions.explain: Anthranilic acid (carboxyl pKa 4.85) is the exception: the strong +R amino group and zwitterion formation outweigh the steric ortho effect.

questions.q: Arrange in decreasing acid strength: o-nitrobenzoic acid (I), o-toluic acid (II), o-chlorobenzoic acid (III), benzoic acid (IV).
questions.explain: The pKa values are 2.2 (I), 2.9 (III), 3.9 (II) and 4.2 (IV), matching the ortho-group order −M > −I > +I; every ortho group here strengthens the acid relative to benzoic acid.
